channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: STF exclui da pauta desta quarta julgamento sobre eleição para mandato-tampão no Rio de Janeiro
item.description: Supreme Court President Edson Fachin removed from today's session agenda the ruling that would define the electoral model for the interim governorship in Rio de Janeiro, to be held until January 2027. Acting Governor Ricardo Couto currently holds the position.

item.title: Investigação no Maranhão chega ao coração do governo Brandão
item.description: The investigation in Maranhão has revealed alleged bribery schemes involving Governor Carlos Brandão, with testimonies linking the crime to disputes over financial 'settlements,' including the claim that the 2022 murder of João Bosco was motivated by this context. Minister Flávio Dino’s decision to lift part of the seal on the case files expanded the scope of the inquiry, which now includes allegations of parliamentary amendment diversions and reaches the core of state power. Meanwhile, in the 2026 presidential race, Lula is gaining an advantage over Flávio Bolsonaro in TV and radio propaganda time, with 5 minutes and 32 seconds versus 4 minutes and 20 seconds, reflecting the strength of his broad coalition.

item.title: Haddad diz que Flávio Bolsonaro é 'grave risco institucional' e não pode conceber derrota de Lula, em sabatina O Globo/CBN/Valor
item.description: Fernando Haddad, the PT's candidate for governor of São Paulo, described Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential candidacy as a "grave institutional risk," stating he cannot conceive of the possibility of him assuming the presidency. He emphasized economic, social, and international risks tied to Flávio Bolsonaro and reiterated that his São Paulo campaign does not jeopardize Lula's national strategy, but instead aims to strengthen the opposition project against Bolsonarism and the centrão.

item.title: Com que roupa Lula vai às urnas? (por Hubert Alquéres)
item.description: Lula is resorting to anti-system rhetoric in his 2026 campaign, despite having become a central figure in Brazil's political establishment since the early 2000s. The article notes that after abandoning the PT’s initial ideological purity in favor of pragmatism and alliances with regional oligarchies and economic sectors, Lula built his power by maintaining neoliberal pillars such as primary surplus and inflation targets. His attempt to present himself as 'new' contrasts with his long trajectory of integration into the system, marked by agreements with figures like Sarney, Renan, Barbalho, and even Michel Temer.

item.title: STF adia definição sobre mandato-tampão no Rio de Janeiro
item.description: The Supreme Federal Court (STF) postponed the judgment on the 'mandato-tampão' in Rio de Janeiro, which concerns whether a direct or indirect election should be held for governor following the resignation of Cláudio Castro and the removal of Rodrigo Bacellar. The case was removed from the agenda to prioritize the review of whether the Maria da Penha Law applies to violence against women without familial or affective ties, and due to the inauguration of the new STJ president. The proximity of the 2026 general elections makes a new state election unlikely.

item.title: STF tira de pauta julgamento sobre eleições para governador no RJ
item.description: Supreme Federal Court (STF) President Justice Edson Fachin removed from the agenda the judgment on how the Rio de Janeiro governor should be elected — either by direct or indirect vote. The preliminary score stood at 4–1 in favor of indirect election via the state legislature (Alerj), with Justices Luiz Fux, André Mendonça, Nunes Marques, and Cármen Lúcia supporting that option, while Cristiano Zanin advocated for direct popular vote. The deliberation was postponed due to the proximity of the October general elections and replaced by a case concerning the application of the Maria da Penha Law to gender-based violence in public or professional settings without familial ties.

item.title: Garagem dos presidenciáveis vai de moto de R$ 7 mil a Land Rover de R$ 376 mil
item.description: The asset declarations of 2026 presidential candidates show wide disparity in vehicle ownership, ranging from a R$ 7,100 motorcycle (Ronaldo Caiado) to a R$ 376,000 Land Rover (Clariana Barão). Some candidates, like Lula, retain donated vehicles with outdated values, while others, such as Pablo Marçal, display luxury cars not officially declared. Electoral law does not require value updates, making declarations reflect historical, not current, asset status.

item.title: Deputado do PL vira réu no STF por desejar morte de Lula
item.description: Federal Deputy Gilvan da Federal (PL-ES) has been made a defendant in the STF after the First Chamber unanimously accepted the PGR's indictment for injuring President Lula, based on offensive statements made in April 2025, including expressing a desire for the president's death, disseminated during a Congressional session and on social media. Justice Cármen Lúcia lifted parliamentary immunity, stating that constitutional protection does not extend to acts performed after the mandate, especially when the legislator amplifies dissemination outside the legislative environment. The decision was unanimous, with Justices Alexandre de Moraes and Flávio Dino supporting the rapporteur's vote.

item.title: Investidor estrangeiro tem maior fuga semanal da bolsa em 18 anos
item.description: Foreign investors withdrew R$12.6 billion from Brazil's stock market in the week of August 10–14, the largest weekly outflow since 2008, driven by electoral and fiscal uncertainties beyond 2027. Analysts cite pressure on interest rates, food inflation risks from El Niño, and weak corporate earnings as factors boosting caution and capital flight. The market expects heightened Ibovespa volatility as elections draw near.

item.title: Governo repassa R$ 251 milhões em crédito suplementar para USP
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas signed a decree allocating R$ 251.1 million in supplementary credit to the University of São Paulo (USP) for purchasing supplies and covering operational expenses, with R$ 251 million coming from state taxes and R$ 180 thousand from USP’s own revenue. The transfer is part of a year-end budget reallocation permitted under the Annual Budget Law and took effect immediately.

item.title: Haddad minimiza custo das câmeras nas fardas, fala em sucateamento das delegacias e propõe B.O 'por zap', em sabatina do Globo/CBN/Valor
item.description: Fernando Haddad criticized Tarcísio de Freitas' security policy, citing an 80% increase in police lethality and the alleged waste of R$600 million on the Muralha Paulista. He advocated for reinstating body-worn cameras on police officers, arguing the cost is minimal compared to lives saved, and proposed a WhatsApp-based police report system enhanced by artificial intelligence to gather detailed incident information for data-driven policing and investigation.

item.title: Flávio também não vai ao debate da Band?
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) announced he will not attend the Band presidential debate scheduled for August 23, following President Lula’s (PT) decision to skip the event. His political coordinator stated that Flávio will only participate in debates where Lula is also present, out of respect for other candidates. The move highlights a strategic alignment between Flávio’s campaign and Lula’s, despite their opposing party affiliations.

item.title: Diálogo entre instituições não significa interferência, diz Nunes Marques
item.description: Minister Kassio Nunes Marques, president of the TSE, stated that dialogue between the Electoral Justice and the TCU does not imply interference but represents a harmonious control model, where the TCU provides technical proof of budgetary violations and the TSE applies political sanctions of candidacy ineligibility. He emphasized that the TCU's list of over 6,100 officials with irregular accounts from the past eight years assists in evaluating candidacies for the 2026 elections. The initiative underscores the complementarity between public resource control and electoral integrity as democratic pillars.

item.title: Lula é aprovado por 54% e desaprovado por 45% no DF, diz pesquisa
item.description: The Real Time Big Data survey conducted between August 14 and 18, 2026, in the Federal District shows that 54% of voters approve of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's work, while 45% disapprove. In detailed evaluation, 30% rate the government as excellent or good, 39% as regular, and 29% as bad or terrible. The survey interviewed 1,600 voters, has a margin of error of 2 percentage points, and a 95% confidence level.

item.title: Lula registra primeiras doações de campanha; veja valores
item.description: President Lula has reported the first campaign donations for his re-election bid, totaling R$500. Campaign treasurer José de Filippi Jr., former mayor of Diadema (SP), donated R$300, and Deivid Ferreira Couto, former aide to a São Paulo state PT deputy, contributed R$200. The amounts were formally declared in the TSE system.

item.title: Quem é a candidata a deputada federal do PL-SP que ganha Bolsa Família
item.description: Sophia Barclay, a federal deputy candidate for PL-SP, is a Bolsa Família beneficiary known for her anti-woke stance and opposition to Erika Hilton. She faced defamation lawsuits from Flávio Bolsonaro and Neymar over false claims of sexual relations, later issuing public retractions. Her campaign highlights right-wing activism and cultural warfare.

item.title: Luis Felipe Salomão assume presidência do STJ em cerimônia com Lula, Alcolumbre e Fachin
item.description: Minister Luis Felipe Salomão assumes the presidency of the Superior Tribunal of Justice (STJ) in a ceremony scheduled for March 19, formalizing the 2026-2028 administration. The event will feature President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, Senate President Davi Alcolumbre, and STF President Edson Fachin, marking the end of Herman Benjamin’s tenure. Salomão was unanimously elected in April 2024, alongside Mauro Campbell Marques as vice-president, concluding over 30 years of judicial service.

item.title: Flávio tem 44% e Lula, 39%, no DF, diz Real Time Big Data
item.description: The Real Time Big Data poll from August 2026 shows Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) leading with 44% in the presidential runoff in the Federal District, against 39% for Lula (PT). In the first round, they are technically tied at 35% and 36%, with Renan Santos and Ronaldo Caiado tied at 8%. Lula has the highest rejection rate (48%), followed by Flávio at 40%.

item.title: Advogado de Lulinha rebate Gaspar: “PF está mais perto da porta dele”
item.description: The lawyer for Fábio Luís da Silva, known as Lulinha, rebutted the claim by Alfredo Gaspar, running mate of Flávio Bolsonaro, that Lula’s son will be arrested by the Federal Police. Marco Aurélio de Carvalho suggested Gaspar is closer to being investigated and questioned his mental capacity, emphasizing there is no basis for arresting Lulinha’s detention — currently residing in Spain — or, potentially, that of Marcola.

item.title: O dado das pesquisas do PL mais comemorado na campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The PL leadership celebrated the party's latest internal tracking polls, which show the smallest gap ever recorded between Flávio Bolsonaro and Lula in voter intention surveys, although the senator still trails numerically behind the president. The exclusive article highlights campaign optimism over the evolving data.

item.title: Por que a amiga de Lulinha ‘abandonou’ a mansão em Brasília?
item.description: Roberta Luchsinger, a lobbyist and friend of Fábio Luís Lula da Silva (Lulinha), son of President Lula, has stopped frequenting the Brasília mansion she rented after being targeted in December by Federal Police searches ordered by the Supreme Federal Tribunal. The property owner confirmed to Globo that she has not returned since, indicating a possible withdrawal linked to ongoing investigations.

item.title: Tarcísio diz que Forças Armadas ‘definham’ e culpa governo Lula por regulamentação das bets
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas accused the Lula administration of allowing the Armed Forces to 'die' and 'wither', undermining national security and organized crime combat. He also criticized the regulation of sports betting by Finance Minister Fernando Haddad, linking it to household debt and retail harm, while affirming his alignment with Bolsonarism, albeit with his own identity.

item.title: JOTA Principal | Após turbulências, aliados de Flávio Bolsonaro avaliam que campanha se estabilizou
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign, after facing initial turbulence — including revelations about his relationship with Daniel Vorcaro, conflicts with Michelle Bolsonaro, and U.S. tariffs — has reportedly stabilized, according to allies. Despite three early setbacks and three changes in campaign managers, the senator unveiled a right-wing government plan focused on combating organized crime and fiscal adjustment, aiming to broaden his appeal beyond the core Bolsonarist base. Investigations and rumors about additional material involving his ties to Vorcaro continue to linger.

item.title: Alvo da PF por suspeita de tráfico de influência, Lulinha tem 18 registros de entrada no Planalto em um ano e meio
item.description: Fábio Luís Lula da Silva, known as Lulinha, had 18 recorded entries into the Planalto Palace between June 2023 and January 2025, according to data obtained via the Access to Information Law. He is under investigation by the Federal Police for suspected influence peddling linked to his association with lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger and former chief of staff Marco Aurélio Santana Ribeiro (Marcola), involving alleged attempts to sell cannabidiol to the Ministry of Health through questionable contracts. Lulinha’s defense claims the visits were solely to see his father, President Lula, and that he did not participate in meetings or discuss government matters.

item.title: Renan Santos diz que bomba atômica dará soberania ao Brasil
item.description: Renan Santos, presidential candidate for the Missão party, advocated for Brazil to acquire nuclear weapons as part of a process to reclaim national sovereignty, proposing withdrawal from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty. He stated that such a move would require coordination with the U.S. and China and be tied to Brazil’s participation in an international arms industry, while noting the country’s existing nuclear fuel cycle capabilities. Santos also promoted political leadership in South America and de-dollarization through a real-led currency basket.

item.title: Tarcísio diz que rechaça "o que não faz sentido" no bolsonarismo
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) stated he identifies with bolsonarism but rejects 'what doesn't make sense' within it, citing São Paulo's increased vaccination coverage as evidence of his pragmatic approach. He also said his administration is reevaluating the mandatory use of educational platforms in public schools, acknowledging potential rigidity in the model, and noted differences between São Paulo and Paraná's education systems. Tarcísio distanced himself from mass incarceration policies supported by allies like Flávio Bolsonaro, despite sharing campaign agendas with him.

item.title: Renan Santos sobre perder cargo por desobedecer STF: "Risco a correr"
item.description: Renan Santos, presidential candidate for the Missão party, stated he would not comply with STF rulings he deems illegal, citing risks to lives in security operations. He said he would accept the consequences, including possible impeachment, and referenced a 1996 ruling by Minister Maurício Corrêa to justify his stance.

item.title: Renan Santos sobre PCC e CV como terroristas: "Efeito de marketing"
item.description: Renan Santos, presidential candidate for the Missão party, labeled the U.S. designation of PCC and CV as terrorist organizations a 'marketing effect', claiming it does not affect Brazil's fight against crime and instead grants the U.S. power to sanction Brazilian companies linked to these groups. He criticized those celebrating the move on social media, saying they are deluded about Trump's friendship with South America.

item.title: Ministro Luís Felipe Salomão toma posse como presidente do STJ; saiba quem é
item.description: Minister Luís Felipe Salomão was sworn in as president of the Superior Court of Justice (STJ) this Wednesday, having previously served as vice-president and national justice corregidor between 2022 and 2024. Before that, he was a minister of the TSE and electoral corregidor in the 2018 and 2020 elections, and has been part of the STJ since 2008, appointed by Lula. His leadership marks the return to secret voting for the STJ presidency, following a period of acclamation.

item.title: Quem é Fernando Cerimedo, antigo estrategista de Milei e aliado de Eduardo Bolsonaro, preso na terça
item.description: Fernando Cerimedo, an Argentine political strategist and ally of Eduardo Bolsonaro, was arrested on Tuesday (18) at Viru Viru International Airport in Santa Cruz de la Sierra, Bolivia, on suspicion of involvement in a shooting attack against his ex-wife. He had previously been investigated in Brazil for spreading false claims about the country's electronic voting system during 2022 live broadcasts that fueled post-election fraud narratives. Although indicted by the Federal Police in the investigation into the alleged coup attempt, Cerimedo was not formally charged by the PGR, which concluded there was insufficient evidence to prove his knowledge and adherence to the coup plot.

item.title: Gaspar, o coringa de Flávio no caso Lulinha
item.description: Alfredo Gaspar (PL-AL) joined Flávio Bolsonaro's ticket, bringing as a trump card his investigation into the INSS scandal, which positioned Lulinha as a central target of the opposition. Although his report was defeated in the CPMI, the information gathered by the commission remains a political weapon in the fight against Lula. The move aims to strengthen Flávio Bolsonaro's narrative based on alleged irregularities involving the former president's son.

item.title: Jornalista se irrita com confusão ao vivo na GloboNews: “Me orientem”
item.description: Journalist Aline Midlej experienced confusion live on GloboNews' Jornal das Dez, receiving conflicting instructions from production about whether to continue an interview with reporter Beatriz Borges or air a video of President Lula. She repeatedly asked for technical guidance, even suggesting a commercial break to reorganize the broadcast, and concluded with humor, saying 'live journalism is like this'. The moment went viral on social media.

item.title: Elevar salário de professores de SP em 1% custaria R$ 500 mi, diz Tarcísio
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas stated that a 1% salary increase for state school teachers would cost nearly R$ 500 million annually, noting the state ranks 16th to 17th nationally in teacher pay. He emphasized that the state employs over 200,000 active teachers, making such adjustments fiscally significant and impacting pensions, while expressing a desire to pay the best teacher salaries in Brazil. Tarcísio also acknowledged criticism regarding classroom technology use, admitting some policies caused rigidity and said the government is revising its approach for greater flexibility.

item.title: Tarcísio diz não concordar com tudo do “bolsonarismo” e cita vacinas
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas said he identifies with bolsonarism but disagrees with certain positions of the movement, explicitly citing vaccine policy as a point of divergence, highlighting his efforts to expand vaccination coverage in São Paulo. He described himself as conservative, liberal, and a believer in a lean state and efficient public service, emphasizing his own identity despite gratitude to Bolsonaro. He confirmed electoral coordination with Flávio Bolsonaro, including joint events such as participation in the Barretos Festival and a lunch scheduled for the same day.

item.title: Eventos esvaziados provocam mal-estar na campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign faced low turnout in its first official events, including a poorly attended 'sticker blast' in Belo Horizonte with only 100 people, a canceled event in Juiz de Fora, and a launch in Copacabana drawing 8,9 thousand — far below historical bolsonarist crowds in the same area. The poor mobilization caused discomfort for the candidate and complaints to his organizing team, led by Vicente Santini, highlighting struggles in grassroots event coordination.

item.title: Haddad inicia série de sabatinas de O Globo/Valor/CBN ao governo de SP; acompanhe ao vivo
item.description: Fernando Haddad (PT) begins today a series of interviews with O Globo, Valor Econômico and CBN as the first candidate for governor of São Paulo, discussing topics such as Sabesp privatization, public security and education. The interview will be conducted by Vera Magalhães, Marcello Corrêa and Guilherme Muniz, lasting 1h30, focusing on the confrontation with Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos). Haddad officially launched his campaign alongside Lula and has criticized the current administration’s management, while Tarcísio will be interviewed on Thursday (20) at the same time.

item.title: MPF processa Renan por “discurso de ódio” contra indígenas
item.description: The Federal Public Ministry has sued presidential candidate Renan Santos (Missão) and the Movimento Brasil Livre for hate speech against 14 indigenous ethnic groups, citing derogatory terms like 'malandros' and 'vagabundos' in Instagram videos. The lawsuit seeks R$ 500 thousand in collective moral damages, removal of the videos, and a public retraction. Renan called the action 'bizarre' and vowed to end what he calls the 'farce' of people claiming indigenous identity.

item.title: Uma mansão para Lulinha e sua amiga lobista em Brasília
item.description: Fábio Luís Lula da Silva, known as Lulinha, son of President Lula, and his friend Roberta Luchsinger, a lobbyist, used a house in Lago Sul, Brasília, for political meetings, according to O Globo. Lulinha is under investigation by the Federal Police for influence peddling in the Planalto Palace. The property, located in an upscale area of the capital, served as a hub for suspected influence activities.

item.title: Flávio decide limitar debates no primeiro turno e só participar quando Lula estiver presente
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL) campaign has decided the candidate will only participate in first-round debates if President Lula (PT) is also present, aiming to avoid becoming the main target of right-wing rivals like Caiado, Zema, and Renan Santos. The strategy seeks to maintain polarization with Lula and prevent Flávio from accumulating attacks from candidates who could become allies in a potential runoff. As a result, Flávio is expected to skip the Band network's televised debate this Sunday, since Lula has not confirmed attendance.

item.title: Novas revelações sobre Lulinha e Marcola incomodam Lula, e PT vai usar contato entre Vorcaro e Flávio Bolsonaro para contra-atacar
item.description: New revelations about alleged connections between Lulinha (Fábio Luís Lula da Silva), former chief of staff Marcola, and lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger are causing embarrassment for President Lula, who denies knowledge and insists his son will testify before the PF. The PT plans to leverage investigations into the alleged misappropriation of R$ 61 million from Daniel Vorcaro for the film 'Dark Horse' — allegedly used to fund Eduardo Bolsonaro’s expenses in the U.S. — as electoral ammunition against Flávio Bolsonaro and the PL.

item.title: Lula e Alcolumbre reabrem diálogo de olho em 2026 e no pós-eleição
item.description: Lula and Alcolumbre re-established dialogue in a dinner hosted by Alexandre de Moraes, focusing on the 2026 elections and approval of agendas like the Public Security PEC and the end of the 6x1 work scale. Despite the rapprochement, no agreement was reached to approve Jorge Messias for the STF, and the meeting served more to adjust political strategies than to achieve personal reconciliation.

item.title: Ao vivo: Nunes Marques e Vital do Rêgo participam de evento no TCU
item.description: The Federal Court of Accounts (TCU) will hold a technical panel on Wednesday, August 19, 2026, at 9:30 a.m., titled 'Impacts of TCU Decisions on Electoral Ineligibility,' featuring TCU President Minister Vital do Rêgo and TSE President Minister Nunes Marques. The event aims to engage key stakeholders on electoral ineligibility arising from the rejection of public accounts, highlighting the TCU’s role in electoral oversight.

item.title: Ao vivo: Lula vai ao Centro Industrial Nuclear de Aramar, em Iperó
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) visits the Industrial Nuclear Center of Aramar in Iperó, São Paulo, to oversee the assembly of the reactor intended for Brazil’s future nuclear-powered submarine. The visit underscores commitment to the Navy’s Nuclear Program, aimed at mastering the nuclear fuel cycle and developing technologies for naval energy generation. The event takes place on Wednesday, August 19, 2026.

item.title: Tarcísio diz que eleição de Flávio facilitaria vida de SP e prevê eventos conjuntos
item.description: São Paulo Governor and re-election candidate Tarcísio de Freitas said that electing Flávio Bolsonaro as president would facilitate relations between the state government and the federal government. He confirmed they will participate in joint campaign events, as stated in a Jovem Pan News interview.

item.title: Zema faz ação em feira de São Paulo e participa de sabatina do SBT
item.description: Romeu Zema, the Novo party's presidential candidate, participates in an action at the Guaianases Market in São Paulo's eastern zone to discuss food inflation. Later that evening, he will be interviewed by SBT News and SBT teams.

item.title: Ex-presidente de banco apoia Renan Santos e ajuda a abrir portas no mercado financeiro
item.description: Former bank president José Olympio Pereira, 64, has announced his support for Renan Santos' (Mission) presidential candidacy and is helping the candidate establish connections in the financial sector. His experience at major banking institutions is seen as an asset to strengthen the economic credibility of the campaign.

item.title: Encontro na Câmara celebra cinco anos do Observatório Nacional da Mulher na Política
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies is celebrating the five-year anniversary of the National Observatory of Women in Politics with an event in the Freitas Nobre auditorium, highlighting its work in producing data on political violence, legislative productivity, and female electoral participation. Created in June 2021, the Observatory has produced over 30 publications and maintains a monitoring system with data from 2002 onward.

item.title: Corrupção do INSS chegou ao gabinete de Lula, diz Flávio
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro accused President Lula of having INSS corruption inside his cabinet, claiming that the president's son, Fábio Luís da Silva (Lulinha), used paternal influence to facilitate business in ministries, including Health, through Marco Aurélio Santana Ribeiro (Marcola), former chief of staff. He also accused lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger of buying jewelry for Marcola, linking the case to alleged INSS fraud involving lobbyist 'Careca do INSS', Antonio Carlos Camilo Antunes, already arrested by the PF.

item.title: Juliano Spyer reúne jornalistas e acadêmicos em lançamento de livro em SP
item.description: Anthropologist and Folha columnist Juliano Spyer launched his new book, 'The Brazil of Evangelicals', at an event held at Livraria da Vila on Paulista Avenue in São Paulo on Monday, the 17th. The launch featured former SBT journalism director Marcos Wilson and other journalists and academics in attendance.

item.title: Tarcísio: Me identifico com bolsonarismo, mas rechaço o que não faz sentido
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas, the Republican candidate for re-election as governor of São Paulo, said he identifies with Bolsonarism but rejects positions he considers illogical. He cited the state’s vaccination campaign as an example of a policy he supports despite ideological differences. He is participating in a morning interview on Jovem Pan today.
